Expectation1: Listen actively and provide emotional support when needed.
Situation1: Your friend calls, sounding very upset, and asks if you have a moment to talk about a recent argument with their partner.
Expectation2: Review and analyze legal documents and contracts
Situation2: A purchase agreement needs analysis before an upcoming filing deadline that is drawing nearer.
Story:
My phone buzzed just as I was about to dive into the thick stack of documents on my desk. It was Jamie, my oldest friend, and her voice trembled as she asked if I had a moment. She needed to talk—her partner had said something hurtful, and she was unraveling. I could hear the tears she was trying to hold back. Instinctively, I wanted to drop everything, listen, and be the friend she needed, the one who always made time for her no matter what.

But the purchase agreement on my desk glared at me, a silent reminder of the looming deadline. If I didn’t review it now, I risked missing crucial details that could cost my client dearly. My mind raced, torn between the duty to my profession and the loyalty to my friend. I could almost feel the weight of both expectations pressing down on me, my heart aching for Jamie while my brain screamed about the consequences of neglecting my work. I gripped the phone tighter, caught in the impossible space between being the friend she needed and the lawyer I was expected to be.
